subject: EdgeWave Dedicated: GPU selection & capacity path

Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: which GPU mix for EdgeWave?

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. Quick intro: EdgeWave is evaluating a Dedicated deployment for inference (non-public data) and we want guidance on GPU SKU selection. Two main surface areas:

1) Embeddings-heavy search index refreshes (90% of calls): open-encoder-1536 style vectors, batch embeddings jobs overnight + 300 TPS during business hours for realtime indexing. Small model footprint, high qps.

2) Multimodal / chat summarization and reranking (10%): a decoder model we run with long context windows (up to 64k tokens in some workflows) for document summarization and customer chat. Latency SLOs: p95 generation under 800ms for interactive flows; background batch summaries can be slower.

Constraints:
- Budget is sensitive; procurement will prefer a predictable monthly commit but we want to avoid huge overprovisioning.
- We may need on-prem routing for a pilot region (US-East).

Questions:
- From your experience, how should we split H100/A100/L4 across these two workloads?
- What are the memory vs perf tradeoffs we should care about (esp for 64k context runs)?
- Any recommended fallback paths (e.g., A100 for long-context failover, L4 for embeddings) and rough cost delta?

Happy to share more metrics (avg tokens per call, batch sizes). Can you send a short recommended path we can use in the procurement deck?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
EdgeWave

Attachment: edgewave_inference_profile.csv (schema: endpoint, avg_qps, p95_latency_ms, avg_tokens_in, avg_tokens_out, batch_window_min)

Samir —

Appreciate the concise profile. I've attached a quick capacity template that will help us convert the metrics into GPU-hours and an initial cost estimate. High-level guidance up-front so you can include it in the procurement deck:

- Embeddings (high QPS, low memory): L4 is typically the most cost-effective for large embedding fleets when models are quantized to INT8/4-bit. Autoscaled L4 pools for realtime indexing + scheduled larger batching clusters for nightly refreshes often hit a good cost point.

- Long-context summarization (64k): H100-class cards (large VRAM + NVLink/4x M.2 support) are the safest primary choice for single-node long-context runs with KV cache and large activation memory. A100 is capable too but you'll see larger quantization tradeoffs and possibly multi-GPU sharding for >40k contexts.

- Middle ground / burst / fallback: A100 is the balanced option for typical gen workloads and can act as a failover for H100 if you configure model variants (reduced context or quantized weights).

Quick asks: can you populate avg_tokens_in/out and concurrency targets for the summarization endpoint? That will let us size H100s vs A100s precisely.

I'll run a short internal sketch and loop back with a proposed initial fleet split + rationales.

—Connor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity ask: which GPU mix for EdgeWave? — proposed SKU path

Forwarding Samir's profile. Key asks: embedding-heavy + occasional 64k summarization. Draft recommendation below; please weigh in on numbers/costs and whether we should propose a staged commit.

=== Draft recommendation (initial committed capacity + burst) ===
Assumptions from follow-up call:
- Embedding qps during daytime: 300 rps (avg batch size 8) => ~2.4k embeddings/sec
- Nightly batch embed jobs: peak aggregate throughput target equivalent to 10k embeddings/sec for 4 hours
- Summarization: 5 concurrent interactive sessions at p95 <= 800ms; avg generation ~600 tokens out, avg input ~12k tokens; occasional 64k runs (1-2/day, batch)

Proposed fleet (US-East pilot):
- L4 pool: 6 x L4 (dedicated to embeddings)
  - Rationale: L4 optimized for dense INT8 inference, best $/embedding. Handles high concurrent small requests and efficient batching.
- A100 pool: 6 x A100 (general gen + fallback)
  - Rationale: Good mid-range memory (40–80GB variants) and throughput for typical generation and smaller context windows; cheaper than H100. Used for burst overflow from L4 (if model variant available) and for regular gen when H100 is occupied.
- H100 pool: 3 x H100 (primary for long-context summarization)
  - Rationale: Higher memory headroom for 64k contexts and better FP16/AMP kernel performance; reduces sharding complexity and keeps latency predictable.

Sizing notes and math (rough):
- Embedding throughput: a single L4 slot (quantized embed model) ~ 400 embeddings/sec (realistic with batching); 6 units -> ~2.4k/s inline with daytime target, plus overnight batching cluster handled via ephemeral burst policy.
- Long-context summarization: H100 single-card generation perf for large-context (12k->600 tokens) ~ 30-40 tokens/sec baseline per card in safe config; at 5 concurrent interactive sessions we get target headroom with 3 H100s when combined with batching and caching (prefix and KV reuse).
- A100 as fallback: A100 will require either aggressive quantization (quality impact) or multi-GPU sharding for very large contexts. Use A100 for short-context fallthrough and non-critical batch workloads.

Cost considerations:
- Recommend committed reservation for L4 pool (predictable usage) + a smaller committed band for A100 with H100 as reserved + optional burst capacity. This reduces unit costs while giving headroom.

Operational recommendations:
- Model variants: publish two inference variants per endpoint — full-context (H100 optimized) and compact (A100/L4 optimized) with explicit routing policies.
- Smart routing: p95-sensitive requests -> route to H100 pool; embeddings -> L4. If H100 is at capacity and request is non-critical, route to A100-compact with reduced context.
- KV/prefix caching: enable persistent KV cache for summarization to reduce re-computation on repeated document slices. This can cut tokens/sec demand by 15–30% depending on repeat access.

Questions for procurement doc:
- Minimum committed months? (we usually suggest 6–12 months for favorable pricing)
- On-prem constraints for pilot? If networking/KMS will be different we should note potential appliance differences.

Tagging cost: I'll produce a tabulated XLS with hourly $/card, estimated monthly hours, and net monthly cost under a 6-month commit for your deck.

—Connor

-- laura_bennett added:
I agree with the mix. Two additions:
1) Put a soft cap on H100 concurrency by queueing interactive runs >5s to preserve latency SLOs.
2) Include an ops playbook for fallback (auto-shed to compact models, sticky sessions to same card for KV reuse).

— Aditya: can you draft the XLS with cost lines (list price vs committed)?
